title: Multiscale Dual-Attention SwinUNet for High-Resolution Aboveground Biomass Estimation With Multisource Data
content: Aboveground biomass (AGB), a key biophysical variable characterizing terrestrial carbon stocks and carbon-cycle processes, is of critical importance for refined carbon accounting, ecological assessment, and ecosystem monitoring. High-resolution AGB estimation relying on a single remote sensing data source often fails to simultaneously capture spectral responses and structural differences of vegetation, and is susceptible to saturation effects and variations in observation conditions, thereby limiting cross-region robustness and generalization. Moreover, for high-resolution AGB estimation using multisource remote sensing data fusion, existing models still suffer from three prominent limitations: a lack of adaptive identification and reweighting of heterogeneous input channels, insufficient multiscale feature interaction and detail reconstruction, and limited capability to explicitly model strong spatial heterogeneity with effective spatial focusing. To address these issues, we propose an improved multiscale dual-attention network, termed MSDA-SwinUNet, built upon SwinUNet. Specifically, a multiscale nested decoder is introduced to strengthen cross-scale semantic interaction and reconstruction, while a channel reweighting attention (CRA) module and a grouped spatial reweighting attention (GSRA) module are embedded in the encoder-coupling and decoder-reconstruction stages, respectively, to enable effective multisource feature selection and enhanced representation of spatial heterogeneity. Experimental results show that MSDA-SwinUNet achieves the best overall performance on the test set, with an R2 of 0.63, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 35.58 Mg/ha, and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 46.65 Mg/ha, indicating that it provides an effective deep-learning solution for high-resolution AGB estimation using multisource data and supports biomass mapping and carbon-monitoring applications.
author: Lingxuan Li, Jiang He, Yuhan Liang, Qiangqiang Yuan

title: TreeSemantic: An Online Module for Individual Tree Segmentation and Attributes Estimation
content: The development of laser scanning (LS) systems and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms has rapidly advanced in recent years. Their integration enables the efficient capture of the 3-D structure of forests, but the attribute estimation at the individual tree level typically requires postprocessing in professional software. To address the limitation, this study presents TreeSemantic, an online individual tree segmentation and attributes estimation algorithm. TreeSemantic is designed as an online framework tightly coupled with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-SLAM. It introduces an equivalent projection strategy that converts irregular 3-D point clouds into structured 2-D representations, allowing efficient normal estimation and individual tree segmentation. In addition, a spatiotemporal aggregation mechanism with external and internal consistency verification is developed to incrementally reconstruct individual trees from sequential scans, mitigating incomplete stem observations caused by occlusion and limited viewpoints. Based on the continuously refined tree clusters, the tree location, diameter at breast height (DBH), and stem curve are estimated in real time. Moreover, commonly used forest inventory products, such as the digital elevation model (DEM), tree attributes database, and pointwise labeled data (tree and ground), are generated immediately after TreeSemantic ends. Extensive experiments were conducted on the self-collected Wuhan University (WHU) dataset and the public TreeScope dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that TreeSemantic achieves nearly 100% tree detection and centimeter-level accuracy in tree attribute estimation. More specifically, the DBH RMSE ranged from 3.82 to 7.93 cm, with the relative RMSE from 15.01% to 29.35%. The stem curve evaluation on 137 matched trees yields an average RMSE of 4.82 cm and a Bias of 1.13 cm. Furthermore, the average running times of normal estimation, segmentation, spatial–temporal aggregation, and attribute estimation are 8.52, 23.46, 13.06, and 11.32 ms, respectively, demonstrating millisecond-level efficiency. Comparisons with state-of-the-art methods, including SLAOM, RealtimeTrees, and 3DFin, further demonstrate that TreeSemantic achieves a favorable balance between accuracy, robustness, and real-time capability. Overall, TreeSemantic provides a practical and efficient solution for users, such as farmers, forest managers, or people without any professional knowledge, to obtain individual tree attributes directly during data acquisition without additional postprocessing.
author: Xiaochen Wang, Xinlian Liang

title: LRCS-Mamba: Low-Rank Mamba With Content-Aware Sparse Scanning for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Recently, state space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as a powerful paradigm for hyperspectral image (HSI) classification due to their linear complexity and ability to capture long-range dependencies. However, existing Mamba-based approaches mainly rely on predefined geometric scanning patterns that ignore spatial heterogeneity, leading to spatial–semantic misalignment. Moreover, standard full-rank parameterization in SSMs fails to exploit the intrinsic low-rank structure of HSI. Without structural constraints, redundant state dynamics may propagate noisy responses caused by misaligned input sequences, further limiting the robustness of spectral–spatial representation learning. To address these coupled issues, we propose LRCS-Mamba, a dual-branch Mamba network with content-aware sparse scanning (CASS) and low-rank state-space modeling for HSI classification. Specifically, we design a CASS mechanism that constructs input sequences via center-neighbor spectral affinity and Top- $k$  selection, reducing heterogeneous boundary-pixel contamination before state evolution. To reduce noisy responses during state evolution, we further develop a low-rank SSM (LRSSM) that factorizes the core evolution matrices and constrains state dynamics within a compact latent subspace. Finally, a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) branch and an adaptive dual-branch sparse gating (ADSG) module are integrated to balance global semantics and local textures. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that LRCS-Mamba consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves robust HSI classification performance.
author: Jinliang An, Longlong Dai, Dengru Han, Weidong Zhang, Xiangrong Zhang

title: Joint Inversion of Gravity Anomaly and Seismic Data for Improved Crustal Imaging in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area
content: Satellite-derived gravity observations provide important constraints on subsurface structure variations, but are limited by poor depth resolution and strong nonuniqueness. Integrating gravity data with seismic data offers an effective approach for improving crustal imaging in tectonically complex regions. Compared with single dataset inversions, the joint inversion greatly improves model resolution and reduces inversion nonuniqueness. The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), located in southern China, is a highly urbanized region with a dense population and strong economic activity. In this study, we built a crustal S-wave velocity and density model of the GBA by joint inversion of gravity anomaly and seismic data. The results show that the crustal structure is very complex. In the shallow crust, the crustal model correlates well with major geological units, and the Pearl River Delta exhibits a prominent low-velocity anomaly associated with thick sedimentary layers, reflecting mechanically weak crust. The seismic events are preferentially located in the transition zone between high-velocity and low-velocity anomalies in the upper crust. At 30 km depth, there is a prominent north-south trending high-velocity anomaly, which may be related to the uplift of the Moho interface. These results show that joint inversion of gravity and seismic data provides an effective strategy for crustal imaging in tectonically complex regions and offers improved constraints for seismic hazard assessment.
author: Haopeng Chen, Yannan Zhou, Senyi Hu, Ruirui Fan, Alex Hay-Man Ng, Fang Zou

title: Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based Three-Dimensional Sea-Surface Wavefield Reconstruction From Sparse Point Clouds
content: Wavefield detection is closely linked to the safety development of maritime low-altitude economic activities, such as providing wave parameters for offshore platforms and supporting marine surveying and inspection. This technology also serves as a key generic technology for optimizing various maritime operations. Accordingly, this article presents a novel research on employing 4-D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar mounted on uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) to achieve high-resolution 3-D wavefield detection. To address the challenge of sparse distribution in the sea-surface point clouds, which are derived from sea clutter obtained by mmWave radar, linear wave theory and sparse representation are integrated to facilitate the extraction of wave model parameters. This process culminates in reconstruction of the wavefield within a specified detection range. The results of numerical simulations have demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of this method in multiple aspects. During sea trials, UAV-captured sea-surface images and instantaneous wave height data measured by surrounding buoys are employed as reference data for comparative wavefield analysis. Preliminary findings show that the reconstructed wavefield is highly consistent with the parameters inverted from UAV nadir videos with respect to both sea-surface characteristics and wave statistical parameters. Compared with traditional methods, this approach features flexible working range, rapid response to wave measurement, and low operational and maintenance costs. Consequently, it is expected to be a viable solution for wavefield detection that balances flexibility and measurement accuracy.
author: Haoyang Fan, Fan Ding, Sitao Wu, Zhijie Hu, Weibo Chen, Xiao Wang, Zezong Chen, Chen Zhao

title: SCDE-Net: Strip-Context and Dilation-Enhanced Deep Unfolding Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Deep unfolding networks (DUNs) hold great potential for infrared small target detection (IRSTD) by embedding the domain prior of target-background separation into interpretable multistage architectures. However, the internal operators of representative unfolding architectures for IRSTD are still largely inherited from generic convolutional designs. Specifically, limited spatial perception makes it difficult to jointly handle structured directional clutter and local target contrast, while premature fusion of the separated background and target components weakens the discrimination available to subsequent stages. To address these issues, we propose a strip-context and dilation-enhanced deep unfolding network (SCDE-Net), which tailors the unfolding pipeline to the physical characteristics of infrared imagery. For background estimation, a strip context background module (SCBM) combines local convolution with orientation-aware strip pooling to suppress structured clutter while retaining local detail responses. For target recovery, a dilated context sparse module (DCSM) widens the receptive field via dilated convolutions to exploit local contrast cues. Furthermore, an adaptive residual fusion module (ARFM) retains the separated background and target representations as distinct inputs to learnable reconstruction, preserving component-specific cues for subsequent stages. Extensive experiments and visual analyses on three public benchmarks (IRSTD-1 K, NUDT-SIRST, and SIRST V1) demonstrate the effectiveness of SCDE-Net and illustrate the behavior of its unfolding stages.
author: Mengmeng Zhang, Dan DU, Hongyuan Jing, Huihui Bai

title: Evaluating the Alignment Between GeoAI Explanations and Domain Knowledge in Satellite-Based Flood Mapping
content: The increasing number of satellites has improved the temporal resolution of Earth observation, making satellite-based flood mapping a promising approach for operational flood monitoring. Deep-learning-based approaches for flood mapping using satellite imagery, an important application within geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI), have shown improved predictive performance by learning complex spatial and spectral patterns from large volumes of remote sensing data. However, the opaque decision-making processes of deep learning models remain a major barrier to their integration into critical scientific and operational workflows. This highlights the need for a systematic assessment of whether model explanations align with established domain knowledge in remote sensing. To address this research gap, this study introduces the Alignment between Domain Knowledge and GeoAI Explanation Evaluation (ADAGE) framework. The proposed framework is designed to systematically evaluate how well explanations of deep learning models align with established remote sensing knowledge, particularly regarding the distinctive spectral properties of the Earth’s surface. The ADAGE framework employs a Channel-Group Shapley Additive Explanations method to estimate the contributions of grouped input channels to pixel-level predictions. Experiments on two satellite-based flood mapping tasks demonstrate that the ADAGE framework can: 1) quantitatively assess the alignment between model explanations and reference explanations derived from domain knowledge, 2) reveal that different models, even when trained using the same data and model configuration, exhibit different sensitivities to the input channel groups, leading to different explanations; and 3) help domain experts identify misaligned explanations through the proposed alignment scores. This study contributes to bridging the gap between explainability and domain knowledge in GeoAI for Earth observation, enhancing the applicability of GeoAI models in scientific and operational workflows.
author: Hyunho Lee, Wenwen Li

title: HRN: A Hybrid Recall Network for Crop Classification Using Multisource Time-Series Remote Sensing Data
content: Remote sensing crop classification based on deep learning (DL) plays a crucial role in crop growth monitoring and yield estimation. However, this field still faces several challenges, including the low classification accuracy of single-source remote sensing datasets (SSRSDs) and the limited generalization capability of existing DL methods. To address these issues, this study constructs three multisource remote sensing datasets (MSRSDs). Furthermore, we propose a Recall Guided Fusion (RGF) module and utilize it to develop a hybrid recall network (HRN) tailored for MSRSD-based crop classification. Experimental results show that, first, HRN achieves the best classification performance among all compared methods, with Overall Accuracy (OA), Average Accuracy (AA), and Kappa Coefficient (κ) improved by 0.11%–9.75%, 0.45%–37.31%, and 0.18%–16.09%, respectively. Second, the CBAM and RGF modules effectively enhance the classification accuracy within HRN. Third, compared with SSRSDs, MSRSDs yield higher classification accuracy, and each data type in the MSRSDs contributes effectively to accuracy improvement. Using the Sentinel2 Munich480 experimental area as an example, this study further analyzes the impact of different MSRSD time-series lengths on classification accuracy and identifies the optimal temporal threshold for constructing classification datasets in this region. The findings provide valuable insights for crop classification, yield estimation, and decision-making applications.
author: Pengao Li, Deng Pan, Yong Xie, Haiyang Yu, Zichuang Li, Ping Zhang, Ruili Wang

title: Rock Type Identification From AVIRIS-NG Hyperspectral Data Using a Bidirectional Gated Attention Convolutional Transformer
content: Mineral exploration using hyperspectral data that has high spectral resolution across visible and shortwave infrared wavelengths become an advanced method for recognizing potential mineral-rich zones. This study introduces a novel deep-learning model for identifying rocks that have associated with iron (banded iron formation) and chromite minerals in the Sittampundi region of Tamil Nadu state, India by using airborne visible infrared spectrometer (AVIRIS-NG) air borne hyperspectral data. Initially, the AVIRIS-NG reflectance data are employed by squeeze net architecture to produce clean denoised output data. Subsequently, the denoised image is processed by a chaotic Chebyshev artificial hummingbird optimization algorithm-based bidirectional gated recurrent unit, an optimized deep learning technique used to generate compressed data. The compressed data are analyzed using a dense attentional net model, which reconstructs the data through a reverse dual-level prediction operation. Building on these techniques, a hybrid deep learning model, an optimized bidirectional gated attention enclosed convolutional transformer, is used to identify different kinds of rocks having different minerals. Here, the multiverse optimizer is used to tune the hyperparameters. Finally, the results are explored in two different ways to compare the designed model. First, the hyperspectral data are directly fed to the mineral classification model and the performance is analyzed accordingly. Second, the hyperspectral data undergo different phases like denoising, compression, reconstruction and identification of rocks with the help of the proposed techniques are examined for evaluation. The proposed model accurately identified the rocks of the Sittampundi region with an accuracy of about 98.51% and a specificity of 99.1%.
author: Divya Mohan, Aravinth J, Sankaran Rajendran

title: GNSS Precise Point Positioning Enhanced Mobile Laser Scanning Railway Point Cloud Registration
content: Mobile laser scanning (MLS) is widely used for high-precision measurement of linear infrastructure such as railways. The fusion of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data with MLS is highly valuable for obtaining high-precision point cloud results. Leveraging the advantages of GNSS precise point positioning (PPP), which estimates position using single-receiver observations, we propose a GNSS PPP-enhanced MLS point cloud registration method that operates without ground base stations. The method integrates PPP positions with local semantic features extracted from railway environments, including ballast bed planes, barrier planes, utility poles, and power lines. A coarse-to-fine registration framework is developed, where PPP provides both initial values for interframe translation and global constraints to suppress drift, while semantic features are used to construct rotation matrices, followed by iterative closest point (ICP) for fine registration. Experiments were conducted on a 3-km railway section, where a high-precision laser scanner mounted on a track inspection trolley captured dense point clouds at an effective rate of up to 1 million points per second. Results show that PPP constraints effectively suppress cumulative drift, achieving centimeter-level registration accuracy. The proposed method yields a 2-D root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.048 m and a 3-D RMSE of 0.079 m. Moreover, semantic geometric features significantly improve rotation accuracy, reducing roll and pitch RMSE by 65.5% and 77.4%, respectively. The robustness experiment achieved 2-D and 3-D RMSE values of 0.034 m and 0.069 m on an approximately 5-km railway section. These results demonstrate that the PPP-based strategy combined with semantic geometric constraints can achieve high-precision point cloud registration without ground base stations, offering a cost-effective solution for railway surveying and similar linear infrastructure applications.
author: Guiqiu Xiang, Haojun Li, Xiaoning Su, Yuzhao Li, Liangke Huang

title: A High-Efficiency Diffusion Model-Inspired Network for Pixel-Level Self-Supervised Hyperspectral Anomaly Change Detection
content: Hyperspectral image change detection (CD) has garnered significant attention in the field of remote sensing. A critical task within CD is anomaly CD. Current generative anomaly CD methods, such as diffusion models, typically rely on computationally expensive iterative sampling to extract features, severely limiting their real-time application capabilities. Furthermore, in the absence of labeled data, existing unsupervised algorithms struggle to effectively distinguish subtle target variations from background artifacts caused by shadows or registration errors. To address these challenges, we propose a novel hyperspectral anomaly CD method named efficient latent denoising-inspired network (ELDI-Net). It employs a one-step manifold projection paradigm, achieving high computational efficiency while preserving the noise-robustness advantages of generative models. Specifically, we introduce a one-step latent manifold projection framework that transforms traditional iterative denoising into a deterministic latent mapping via an encoder–projector–decoder architecture, achieving a substantial improvement in inference speed. In addition, a spectral adaptive calibration projection module is constructed, employing channel-adaptive calibration to suppress spectral redundancy while effectively preserving critical features of subtle targets. A bidirectional focus alignment mechanism is designed for implicit semantic denoising under self-supervised conditions, suppressing pseudovariation artifacts through twin cross-prediction. Finally, a GCI strategy is introduced to eliminate directional sensor noise. Experimental results on three datasets demonstrate that the proposed ELDI-Net method achieves superior or highly competitive performance compared to multiple state-of-the-art approaches.
author: Xing Hu, Xiangcheng Liu, Chenxi Guo, Jiaxin Li, Qianqian Duan, Ruijiao Li, Jing Cheng, Dawei Zhang

title: Evaluation of Spaceborne GPS Data Quality and Higher-order Ionospheric Delay Effects on SWARM Precise Orbit Determination in the Severe Geomagnetic Storm on April 23–24, 2023
content: Geomagnetic storms significantly enhance ionospheric electron density, thereby severely influencing ionospheric delay and degrading the quality of spaceborne GPS observations for low Earth orbit satellites. Traditional study rarely focuses on precise orbit determination (POD) during geomagnetic storms using reduced dynamic method. To improve POD accuracy during Geomagnetic storm, this article proposes a new method applying higher order ionospheric (HOI) delay to correct onboard GPS observation using reduced dynamic method, exemplified by geomagnetic storm of April 23–24, 2023 for SWARM mission, characterized by heightened solar activity and increased geomagnetic indices. A comprehensive assessment of spaceborne GPS data quality reveals a marked deterioration in data quality with a close consistency with the geomagnetic indices. The HOI reaches centimeter level, with second-order ionospheric delays in the L1 and L2 bands peaking at 2.8 and 5.9 cm, respectively, and third-order delays reaching up to 0.7 and 1.8 cm. Overlap orbit validation shows that HOI delay correction can effectively improve the POD accuracy of the SWARM-A, B and C satellites. When HOI delay correction data are used in reduced-dynamic orbit determination, the resulting accuracy is higher than that achieved using ionosphere-free combination data, with an improvement on the order of millimeters. These results underscore the critical influence of HOI delay on onboard GPS observation during geomagnetic storms and highlight the necessity for accurate ionospheric modeling in enhancing POD accuracy.
author: Qiaoli Kong, Leru Gao, Shi Wang, Qian Li, Guoli Bo, Lulu Zhang

title: Unrolled Low-Rank Tensor Completion for SAR-Guided Cloud Removal in Multispectral Images
content: We address the challenge of cloud removal in multispectral satellite images (MSIs), where clouds obscure critical spatial and spectral information. Cloud removal aims to reconstruct cloud-free MSIs by recovering both spatial structures and spectral signatures from partially occluded observations. While traditional model-based algorithms provide a strong theoretical foundation and interpretability by explicitly incorporating intrinsic priors, their performance and generalization are often limited by handcrafted formulations, limiting robustness across diverse cloud conditions. In contrast, recent deep learning approaches achieve superior reconstruction performance but often overlook the physical properties of MSIs, such as spectral redundancy, interband correlations, and low-dimensional subspace structures, which are essential for accurate MSI reconstruction. In this work, we propose a deep unrolled tensor completion framework with synthetic aperture radar (SAR)-guided detail injection for MSI cloud removal, effectively integrating model- and data-driven approaches to leverage their complementary strengths. Specifically, we first formulate cloud removal as a joint optimization problem that preserves spectral correlations via low-rank priors while exploiting SAR information, which provides robust structural and textural guidance for restoring spatial details occluded in the optical images. We further introduce implicit regularizers to compensate for modeling inaccuracies in model-based priors and solve the resulting optimization problem using an iterative scheme, which is unfolded into a multistage deep network where each stage represents a single iteration. Experimental results on multiple real and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves superior cloud removal performance with better interpretability compared to state-of-the-art algorithms, while requiring a smaller number of training samples.
